card.band: 8 h. Multi-part scope (auth, refresh, routing, discovery, CLI and config, error paths). A frontier agent finishes the core in some trials but misses refresh and edge-case buckets. A weaker model stops after the happy-path login.
card.cheat: Hard-coding the mock's responses is closed because hidden mocks differ in tokens, endpoints, catalogues and failure timing. No upstream solution exists to copy. The snapshot has no git history.
card.grading: Hidden behavioural tests run through aider's public Coder, models and main() entry points against several differently scripted mock servers (expiry mid-session, rate limits, entitlement errors, streaming and non-streaming, differing model catalogues). Existing aider suite is a regression gate. Score is the fraction of hidden cases passed.
card.reference: Our own implementation, expected about 1200-1800 added lines plus tests. It passes every hidden case by construction. Mock protocol is documented from public behaviour of the Copilot plugins.
card.source: https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/issues/2227 @ 5dc9490 (v0.86.0), Apache-2.0; long-standing issue (118 upvotes, 214 comments), no merged upstream support found

facts.claim: Aider issue #2227 'Feature: Add GitHub Copilot as model provider' exists, opened 2024-11-03, and is still open with labels enhancement and priority
The only maintainer (paul-gauthier) doubted the approach: it would need an undocumented or abused API, Copilot may not sanction it, and he pointed users to litellm instead
No merged aider-side Copilot support is linked from the issue; no maintainer has marked it planned or wontfix
Open PR #4459 (adds github_copilot/ models) is referenced in the issue thread; its current status was not visible on the page
litellm ships a GitHub Copilot provider using OAuth device-code login, with tokens cached under ~/.config/litellm/github_copilot and a GITHUB_COPILOT_TOKEN_DIR override
The litellm Copilot provider handles the device-code flow and token storage that the seed asks aider to build; aider depends on litellm, so this code is present in the image
Repo at 5dc9490 (v0.86.0) has LICENSE.txt, tests/, and the aider/ package; licence type is not shown on the page, so Apache-2.0 relies on the GitHub API spdx field
The mock Copilot protocol is 'documented from public behaviour of the Copilot plugins'; no public protocol specification for the token exchange or endpoint routing was found
Seed claim 'No upstream solution exists to copy' is contradicted: a working Copilot device-flow and routing implementation is public in litellm, which is installed with aider

spike_plan.kill_if: Litellm's provider covers device-flow, token exchange and refresh as shipped, so the reference is recoverable from the image (confirms K11).
spike_plan.pass_if: Litellm's provider is confirmed to be the only auth path, and a stub run shows the aider-side work left is a small remainder (under about 300 lines); a re-scoped aider-side idea would then be worth a new seed.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, install aider at 5dc9490 (v0.86.0) in a venv and note the pinned litellm version.
Read the installed litellm github_copilot provider source (device-flow, token exchange, refresh, endpoint and header routing) and list which seed buckets it already covers.
Run aider with a github_copilot/ model against a local stub server that mimics the seed's token exchange, to see whether the aider-side wiring works with no new code.
Check open PR #4459 status and whether it changes aider's model list or settings.
Decide: if litellm covers auth and the aider-side work is under about 300 lines, kill (K11). If the task is rebuilt to be aider-side only, re-scope and re-score.

v1.summary: The seed targets a real, long-open aider feature request (#2227, Apache-2.0), but the litellm dependency already implements the Copilot device-flow and token logic, so the seed's sealing and novelty claims fail. The idea is killed as K11 (cannot be sealed) unless it is re-scoped to aider-side routing and CLI work that litellm does not supply.
